significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) signed relation—at matched intrinsic difficulty and comprehension, query language conditions reasoning length and stopping, with low-resource or typologically distant languages tending toward "UNDERTHINK" and some other languages toward overthinking—plus a causal decomposition in which a "shared, language-agnostic difficulty estimate" is distinct from a steerable effort controller. This establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanism, constraining whether multilingual errors should be explained or addressed through comprehension, competence, or inference-budget allocation; that distinction matters given the cross-language reasoning gaps documented by Shi et al., "Language Models are Multilingual Chain-of-Thought Reasoners" (ICLR 2023), and the English-centered latent representations analyzed by Wendler et al., "Do Llamas Work in English?" (ACL 2024). The negative branch is informative insofar as failure of added effort or budget steering would rule out effort misallocation as a material explanation, although it would not by itself fully discriminate comprehension failure from inadequate reasoning competence; true and false outcomes are nevertheless clearly distinguishable. Substitution check: replacing this specific shared-difficulty/language-set-budget decomposition with the generic multilingual-representation topic would not justify the score, because the signed length–accuracy relation and competing causal explanations would disappear.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "effort-budget direction," an inference-time intervention that can "re-allocate reasoning length per language and recover accuracy without retraining," together with reasoning length and early stopping as diagnostic quantities. It is ex ante rather than merely post hoc because it can lengthen or shorten reasoning before the model stops and produces the failure, giving model developers and deployment auditors an action window. After per-model re-extraction, the claim predicts more than the existence of another direction: at matched difficulty, the direction should recover a signed language-conditioned underthinking/overthinking pattern, although it gives no precise transferable scaling law or universal threshold. The hypothesis is stated across multilingual LLMs and language-resource or typological-distance conditions, with uptake by inference-control and multilingual deployment practitioners; substitution check: the broad topic alone supplies neither this control knob nor its lead time, so the reach score comes from the claim-specific handle.
